articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5 in mid-August 2026, featuring deeply integrated chain-of-thought reasoning and the ability to natively generate images, audio, and code artifacts in a single inference pass. The model demonstrates substantial gains on graduate-level science benchmarks and real-world agentic task completion, narrowing the gap between AI assistants and autonomous software engineers.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Multimodal Scientific Reasoning
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2 with a two-million-token context window and improved scientific reasoning capabilities, scoring record results on GPQA Diamond and novel protein-function prediction tasks. The model is being integrated across Google Cloud's Vertex AI platform, giving enterprise customers access to advanced multi-step research workflows.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool-Use Orchestration Framework for Enterprise Agents
articles.summary: Anthropic released a new agentic orchestration layer for Claude that allows enterprises to define complex multi-tool workflows with built-in safety constraints and audit trails. The framework supports sandboxed code execution, database queries, and API chaining while maintaining constitutional AI guardrails, targeting regulated industries like finance and healthcare.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Manufacturing Lines
articles.summary: Tesla confirmed that its third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has started performing repetitive assembly and materials-handling tasks at two of its U.S. Gigafactories. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and on-device vision-language models for real-time task adaptation, though Tesla acknowledged the robots still require human supervisory oversight.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Logistics Warehouses
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics officially launched the commercial version of its electric Atlas humanoid robot, targeting warehouse logistics and heavy-parcel manipulation use cases in partnership with Hyundai's supply chain division. The platform includes a fleet-management SDK and simulation-to-real transfer pipeline, allowing operators to train new manipulation behaviors in digital twins before deploying to physical hardware.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C to Scale Humanoid Robot Production
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a massive $1.5 billion funding round led by Microsoft and Nvidia to scale manufacturing of its Figure 02 humanoid robot for commercial deployment. The company plans to open a dedicated production facility in South Carolina and is targeting 1,000 units deployed across logistics and manufacturing partners by mid-2027.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC announced the start of volume production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors, delivering an estimated 15% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over its N2 node. The first customers are expected to be Apple and Nvidia, with AI accelerator and mobile SoC designs taping out for early 2027 products.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance to Expand Brain-Computer Interface Trials to 50 Patients
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to expand its N1 brain-computer interface clinical trial from a small initial cohort to 50 patients with spinal cord injuries and ALS. Early trial data showed participants achieving cursor control speeds approaching 90% of able-bodied benchmarks, representing a significant milestone for assistive neurotechnology and direct neural-to-device communication.
